extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, and others interested in submitting books to or learning about the National Book Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Information page describing the National Book Awards program: its purpose, the categories it honors, resources for eligibility and submission, and recognition (medallions). Useful for authors, publishers, and nominators preparing submissions or researching the awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories honored
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards currently honor the best Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Translated Literature, and Young People’s Literature, published each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the named genres/categories the National Book Awards recognizes; entries should fall into one of these categories to be considered for the corresponding prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / scope of the awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Book Awards were established in 1950 to celebrate the best writing in America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The National Book Foundation's mission is 'to celebrate the best of American literature, to expand its audience, and to enhance the cultural value of great writing in America.' This frames selection emphasis on the quality of writing and contribution to American letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility, deadlines, and submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines & Guidelines: Eligibility, the submissions process, current prizes, guidelines, FAQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page points to separate 'Deadlines & Guidelines' for concrete rules on who/what is eligible, submission mechanics, and timing; specific eligibility criteria and procedural requirements are provided in that linked guidance (not included in this excerpt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medallions and usage rights for honored titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Seals and digital image rights are available for NBA Winner, Finalist, and Longlist titles. In addition to medallions for individual titles, we also offer medallions for 5 Under 35 honorees and Distinguished Contribution to American Letters medalists, which can be used for future or backlist titles, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners, Finalists, Longlisted titles, and certain honorees may receive official seals/medallions and associated digital image rights for marketing and backlist use—use and eligibility for these marks are governed by the Foundation's policies (details on the linked medallions page).
